the mechanisms of neurotoxicity associated with elevated CNS cytokines, particularly IL-6, which is expressed at elevated concentrations in the CNS in a number of disease states, including Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, and AIDS dementia.
the pathophysiological mechanisms by which IL-6 alters NMDA receptor function, calcium influx, and neurotoxicity in developing neurons.

chronic IL- 6 treatment alters NMDA receptor function in cerebellar granular neurons and enhances the neurotoxic effects of NMDA in these neurons, which is consistent with a role for IL- 6 in neuropathological processes involving NMDA receptor activation in the CNS.

The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-6 is a neurotoxin in developing CNS neurons and that it produces a pathological effect on NMDA receptors that may play a role in neuropathology associated with CNS diseases.
the cytokine, IL-6, can alter NMDA receptor function in developing neurons in a manner that can enhance the neurotoxicity associated with NMDA receptor activation.
IL-6 can have a profound effect on NMDA receptor function in neurons and this may contribute to the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative disorders.
